THE HONOURABLE SRI JUSTICE TARLADA RAJASEKHAR RAO  WRIT PETITION No.10072 of 2024 ORDER:
-
The present Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"...to issue a writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents in not paying the compensation towards the One Time Settlement and Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R and R)
benefits to the 92 Project Displaced Families (PDFs) (87 OTS plus 5 R and R) of Vemavaram village of Machavaram mandal i.e., petitioner herein, under Dr.K.L.Rao Sagar (Pulichintala) Project in terms of Award vide Rc.No.517/2008-A, dated 06-09- 2023 r/w. GO.Rt.No.627, Water Resources (R and R-A2) Department, dated 24-09-2015 under Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 as illegal, arbitrary, violative of Art.300-A of the Constitution of India apart from violation of provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and consequently, direct the respondents to release and pay the compensation towards the One Time Settlement and Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R and R) benefits to the 92 Project Displaced Families (PDFs) (87 OTS plus 5 R and R) of Vemavaram village of Machavaram mandal i.e.,petitioner herein,
under Dr. K.L.Rao Sagar (Pulichintala) Project in terms of Award vide Rc.No.517/2008-A, dated 06-09-2023 r/w. sentences.text: The grievance of the petitioners is that the houses of the petitioners were submerged due to Dr.K.L.Rao Sagar (Pulichintala) Project and the petitioners are project displaced families of Vemavaram Village of Machavaram Mandal.
Though orders were passed for payment of compensation under one time settlement and R&R benefits, the respondents have not been paid any compensation.
Hence, present writ petition is filed.

3. Heard Kesava Kumari Nemala, learned counsel for petitioners and learned Assistant Government Pleader for respondents.
4.

Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition has placed on record written instructions dated 23.09.2025, addressed by the Special Collecotr (L.A.), Dr.K.L.Rao Sagar (Pulichintala) Project, Narasaraopet, Palnadu District and the relevant paragraphs are extracted hereunder for effective disposal of the writ petition:
"...It is submitted that during previous financial year 2024-25 bills were prepared and submitted to the Asst. Pay & Accounts Officer, Narasaraopet vide bill bearing no.2024-1779628 dt.25.11.2024 and bill No.2024-2268905 for payment of compensation to the 92 PDFs of Vemavaram Village of Machavaram Mandal.
The Pay & Accounts Officer, Narasaraopet has honour the bill and forwarded to the financial department for financial concurrence.

Both bills were returned by the CFMS portal with a reason that "Bill returned to DDO as per Art.39 & 50 of AP Financial Code,
Vol-1.
The total budget required for PDFs of Vemavaram Village in Rs.8,60,13,520/-.

Out of which an amount of Rs.2,87,61,600/- (Rupees Two Crores eighty seven lakhs sixty one thousands and six hundred only) has been released in the Financial Year 2025- 26 for the 1st quarter under the head of the account 4700-01-00- 11-120-500-502 (R&R) for payment of to the 92 PDFs (87 OTS & R&R and 5 PDFs R&R) of Vemavaram Village of Machavaram Mandal.

Accordingly, bills were prepared for an amount of Rs.2,68,58,647/- (@33% budget to each PDF) and sent to the Pay & Accounts Officer, Narasaraopet vide bill bearing no.2025- 804342,
dt.09.06.2025 and he honor the bill and forwarded to the financial department for financial concurrence.
The bill present status is "Waiting for funds clearance".
Further, an amount of Rs.1,83,38,150/- is shown in the CFMS portal for 2nd quarter.
But, due to technical issue in the CFMS it is shown as "Phase-Il bill types are not allowed, please use NIDHI works bill types...."
5. On perusal of the written instructions it appears that respondents have not disputed the payment of compensation to the petitioners and bills are pending before the concerned authorities.

6. In the case of The D.F.O., South Kheri And Ors. vs Ram Sanehi Singh1, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that when a State decides not to pay the dues with mala fide, with ulterior motives or arbitrarily or when the State avoids payment of the dues with mala fide, with ulterior motives, arbitrarily or when the State discriminates, while making payment dues, such a decision of the State not to pay or such an act of the State of not paying its dues cannot be said to be wholly beyond the reach of Article Shaik Saidamma Saida Bi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127563980/
9 226, for asking the writ Court to do is to force the State to act in accordance with its constitutional obligation by adhering to the letter and spirit of Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India.
7.

sentences.text: In catena of cases, this Court had held that where dispute revolves round questions of fact, the matter ought not to be entertained under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.

In the present case, the respondents have not disputed the payment of compensation to the petitioners for the property acquired and the respondents have manifested in their written instructions that they will pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they are unable to pay the compensation for not allotment of budget.

Therefore, the present Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

However, petitioners are at liberty to file separate application, before appropriate authority,
for payment of interest.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.

6. In the case of The D.F.O., South Kheri And Ors. vs Ram Sanehi Singh1, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that when a State decides not to pay the dues with mala fide, with ulterior motives or arbitrarily or when the State avoids payment of the dues with mala fide, with ulterior motives, arbitrarily or when the State discriminates, while making payment dues, such a decision of the State not to pay or such an act of the State of not paying its dues cannot be said to be wholly beyond the reach of Article Shaik Saidamma Saida Bi vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127563980/
9 226, for asking the writ Court to do is to force the State to act in accordance with its constitutional obligation by adhering to the letter and spirit of Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India.
7.
In catena of cases, this Court had held that where dispute revolves round questions of fact, the matter ought not to be entertained under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
In the present case, the respondents have not disputed the payment of compensation to the petitioners for the property acquired and the respondents have manifested in their written instructions that they will pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they are unable to pay the compensation for not allotment of budget.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the present Writ Petition is disposed of directing the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners within a period of three (03) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
However, petitioners are at liberty to file separate application, before appropriate authority,
for payment of interest.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
